name: Wallfahrtskloster Maria Waldrast
kurzbeschreibung: Maria Waldrast at 1,638 m at the foot of the Serles: Central Europe's highest monastery, Servite pilgrimage site since 1407, and legendary healing spring.
beschreibung:
Overview

The traditional Servite monastery Maria Waldrast is situated in a majestic high-mountain location at 1,638 meters above sea level at the foot of the striking, 2,717-meter-high Serles (“High Altar of Tyrol”) in the northern Wipptal valley. Located in the municipality of Mühlbachl near Matrei am Brenner, Maria Waldrast is considered the highest monastery in Central Europe and one of the oldest and most significant Marian shrines in the entire Alpine region. Surrounded by dense larch and stone pine forests, this traditional pilgrimage site combines deep spiritual contemplation, Baroque church art, and alpine nature experiences against the rock faces of the Stubai Alps. The special location and long history give this place a unique atmosphere.

Route & Requirements

Maria Waldrast can be reached in various ways, each with different requirements. The most comfortable way to arrive is by car via a toll mountain road from Matrei am Brenner directly to the monastery car park. For hikers, there are several options: The historic pilgrim's Way of the Cross from Matrei is a moderately difficult ascent of about 1.5 to 2 hours. Alternatively, a more leisurely option is to take the Serlesbahn cable car from Mieders in the Stubai Valley up to the Koppeneck mountain station (1,600 m), from where a beautiful, almost flat panoramic hiking trail leads to Maria Waldrast in about 45 minutes. This path is suitable for families and less experienced hikers.

Visit & Arrival

The pilgrimage church of Maria Waldrast is freely and cost-free accessible year-round daily from approximately 07:00 to 19:00. The attached traditional Klostergasthof (monastery inn) offers pilgrims and excursionists regional Tyrolean cuisine as well as cozy overnight accommodation. Arrival by car: Via the Brenner motorway A13 (exit Matrei am Brenner) or toll-free on the B182 to Matrei, from there a well-maintained, approximately five-kilometer-long toll mountain road leads up to the large car park directly at the monastery (toll approx. €6.00 per car). On foot or by cable car: A popular option is to take the Serlesbahn from Mieders in the Stubai Valley up to the Koppeneck mountain station (1,600 m), from where a wonderful, almost flat panoramic hiking trail leads comfortably to Maria Waldrast in about 45 minutes.

Tips

The monastery church, the monastery inn, and the fountain courtyard are largely barrier-free and accessible with all-terrain strollers; the panoramic hiking trail from the Serlesbahn mountain station Koppeneck is wide, gravelled, and family-friendly. Bring empty water bottles to fill up with fresh, energized Waldrast healing water for your hike. In winter, an approximately five-kilometer-long natural toboggan run down to Matrei invites you to thrilling descents, promising a special experience. Take your time to enjoy the tranquility and spiritual atmosphere of this special place and let the impressive mountain landscape work its magic on you. A visit to the Waldrast spring is a must for every visitor.
oeffnungszeiten: Pilgrimage church daily 07:00–19:00; Inn in summer daily, in winter Thu–Sun
